pageTitle: Big Food Group Sauce Bottling Line
headline: Every bottle of sauce checked, not a sample.
label: #FFFFFF
visitLine: Call and visit to your factory
heroLede: Big Food Group makes sauces, dressings and mayonnaise in Melbourne under brands like 8Food and The Original Sauce Company, and packs them for other brands too, in sachets, portion cups, pouches and 500 mL to 1 L bottles. With that many products and customers on one site, the label is what tells one bottle from the next. This is what a camera check could look like on a bottling line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every bottle has its cap on, straight and fully closed. A loose cap means a leak in the carton and a complaint from the customer.
labelLede: A garlic aioli and a sesame dressing can share a bottle and look much the same at line speed, and one of them carries sesame. The camera checks every bottle carries the right label for the run, straight and intact, including on runs for other brands.
codeLede: The best-before and batch code has to be right and readable on every bottle. The system reads the printed code and compares it with the product and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Cap offcuts, label backing and loose parts can end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.

vocab.alert: Four crooked caps in fifteen minutes. Check the capper.
